correctness.rationale: Faces satisfy two exact cardinality bounds because a clique is confined to one maximal block. Filtering augmented integral chains by the number of vertices selected in C produces relative summands equal to shifted joins of two simplex skeletons. The skeleton integral homology is the corresponding exterior augmentation lattice; for filtration column j, the only possible total degree is 2(t-1)-j-1. Every homological spectral sequence differential targets a column whose unique potential degree is greater, so all differentials vanish. The free associated-graded groups imply free integral homology and the stated binomial rank formula. Natural equivariance produces signed-subset lattices; rational semisimplicity yields the given character. The supplied standalone programs passed 11 mod-two examples, four exact integer Smith form examples, and 492 signed Lefschetz comparisons; tests are corroborative, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Intersection along a nontrivial complete clique is the first natural chordal clique-sum family beyond a cut vertex; its t-clique-free complexes exhibit nonzero homology in t consecutive dimensions once a,b≥t and s≥t−1. Exact torsion-free integral ranks for all sizes, a proof of the staircase mechanism, and rational symmetry characters supply meaningful structural information not determined by shellability alone. Not a single arbitrary numerical example or a reparametrization of the known apex case.
